I have farmed this small land for many years using the old ways my mother taught me. I cannot afford chemical fertilizer from the agro-dealer, but I will spread some chicken droppings and kitchen ash on the soil as I always do. I will plant my own cassava cuttings and yam setts saved from last season's harvest, and my children and grandchildren will help me clear and weed the plot when they have time. The rains here in the south are plenty and come twice, so God will water the crops for us; we do not need to hire anyone for such a small piece of land.
